questions.explanation: A soliloquy is spoken with no listener present, unlike a monologue, which is addressed to others.

questions.explanation: The sonnet has fourteen lines, whether in the Shakespearean or Petrarchan pattern.

questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds, while assonance repeats vowel sounds within words.

questions.text: A prose narrative shorter than a novel but longer than a short story is called
questions.explanation: The novella occupies the middle ground in length and usually develops a single line of action.

the Igbo village of Umuofia at the coming of the missionaries
a Hausa emirate before the jihad

questions.explanation: An oxymoron yokes two contradictory words together; antithesis balances contrasting ideas in clauses.

questions.explanation: Tragedy traces the protagonist's fall, often through a flaw of character or an error of judgement.

questions.explanation: Theme is the idea explored; plot is the sequence of events through which it is explored.

questions.explanation: Two lines make a couplet, three a tercet, four a quatrain and six a sestet.

questions.explanation: Dramatic irony creates tension because the audience anticipates what the character cannot foresee.

questions.explanation: A metaphor asserts identity between the two things compared; a simile signals the comparison with 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Giving human qualities to inanimate objects or abstract ideas is
questions.explanation: Personification endows non-human things with human attributes, as in 'the wind whispered'.

questions.explanation: Rhyme scheme is expressed with letters such as abab or aabb; metre concerns stress patterns.

questions.explanation: The refrain reinforces mood and theme through repetition.

questions.text: The struggle between opposing forces that drives a narrative is called
questions.explanation: Conflict may be internal, within a character, or external, against others, society or nature.

questions.text: A character who does not change throughout a narrative is described as
questions.explanation: Flat characters are built on a single trait and remain static; round characters develop.

questions.text: In Greek tragedy, the error of judgement that leads to the hero's downfall is
questions.explanation: Hamartia is the tragic flaw or error; hubris, excessive pride, is one common form of it.

questions.explanation: The exposition sets up the situation before the rising action begins.

questions.explanation: Folktales, praise poetry, riddles and proverbs are performed and passed on orally.

questions.explanation: Allusion enriches meaning by calling to mind something outside the text.

questions.text: The use of ridicule to expose folly or vice in society is
questions.explanation: Satire holds human failings up to scorn with the aim of correcting them.
